import pytest
from jinja2 import Environment

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_custom_filter_with_slice_async_true():
    jinja_env = Environment(enable_async=True)
    jinja_env.filters.update({'add_two': lambda x, y: [i + y for i in x]})

    template = jinja_env.from_string("{% for item in (a.b|add_two(5))[:1] %}{{ item }}{% endfor %}")
    data = dict(a=dict(b=[1, 2, 3]))

    # This should render without error and produce the expected output
    result = await template.render_async(data)
    assert result == "6"

    # Test the alternative syntax that currently raises a TemplateSyntaxError
    # This is to ensure that the fix for the original issue doesn't break this case
    # and that the syntax error remains if it's indeed invalid.
    template_syntax_error = jinja_env.from_string("{% for item in a.b|add_two(5)[:1] %}{{ item }}{% endfor %}")
    with pytest.raises(
        jinja_env.exceptions.TemplateSyntaxError,
        match="expected token 'end of statement block', got '\\['"
    ):
        await template_syntax_error.render_async(data)
